summary: No P1/P2 found in this exact two-file candidate. Listener collection owns subscription lifetime. Actual Session lifecycle and inbound MethodChannel event refresh are exercised in authored tests. No Dart/Flutter tests or compiler were run locally.

production_assessment.finding: Registration remains idempotent contains/add and remove. Setter projects caller enabled OR listener collection nonempty. Repeated true calls acquire no synthetic owner; false while any registered Session survives stays true; false with no listener disables.

Real Android Session registers before enable and unregisters before disable. Successful repeated dispose returns cached future and cannot decrement a count twice. Setter adds no mutable enabled cache, refcount, or ACK-dependent ownership.

Unchanged Java method applies registration synchronously before success reply; native registration/unregistration is idempotent. Flutter built-in MethodChannel documented FIFO plus this synchronous application makes delayed ACK distinct from a delayed false call. New false calls re-read current Dart listeners before dispatch.

invokeMethod<void> matches setter Future<void> contract and unchanged native null success reply. Caller errors remain Future failures, so explicit retries are possible; existing Session best-effort catchError behavior is unchanged.

First setter use initializes actual inbound MethodCall handler. Handler snapshots listeners and Session callback re-queries its target/source. Tests use this real path through forTesting provider, not an injected replacement callback dispatcher.

authored_test_assessment.name: disposing one Session preserves the surviving capability refresh
authored_test_assessment.evidence: Two real forTesting Sessions. Disposing A keeps nativeEnabled true; incoming Changed encoded through actual TestDefaultBinaryMessenger invokes surviving B capability provider and yields B HdrCapabilityChangedEvent. A provider remains 0, B becomes 1. Repeated A dispose sends no extra call, final B dispose sends false. Old forwarded-false implementation fails direct keepsSubscription/nativeEnabled assertion before event wait.

authored_test_assessment.name: listener registration and repeated enables do not count extra owners
authored_test_assessment.evidence: One real surviving Session plus same manual listener registered twice; remove succeeds once only. Repeated explicit true adds no retained owner; false preserves real Session and final dispose closes.

authored_test_assessment.name: a late disable cannot unsubscribe a replacement Session
authored_test_assessment.evidence: Previous last Session disposes, replacement registers. A deliberately late setter false is dispatched while replacement lives and projects true. Final replacement dispose still closes.

authored_test_assessment.name: a delayed native acknowledgement does not retain a disposed owner
authored_test_assessment.evidence: First enable applies immediately at mock receipt while its ACK Future is held. Second Session lives through first dispose. Releasing ACK introduces no ghost ownership; final dispose closes.

authored_test_assessment.name: native failures preserve current ownership and permit a retry
authored_test_assessment.evidence: Explicit false with real owner projects true, returns PlatformException before mock apply; retry preserves true. Last real Session.dispose then sends false but failure leaves native enabled under existing caught-error behavior. Explicit false fails again, then successful retry disables. Recorded booleans true,true,true,false,false,false.

test_harness_assessment: Mock mutates nativeEnabled on receipt, before awaiting an optional held ACK. The injected synchronous exception occurs before native apply; this does not model impossible late mutation after later FIFO calls.

Helpers subscribe to broadcast nativeCalls before construction/disposal, so synchronous native receipt is not missed. First inbound-event test asserts subscription true before awaiting provider event, so baseline bug fails directly.

TestDefaultBinaryMessengerBinding.instance.defaultBinaryMessenger is statically TestDefaultBinaryMessenger. Its handlePlatformMessage returns Future<ByteData?> and null callback is supported. Base BinaryMessenger Future<void> signature does not apply to inferred messenger. No compile-blocking use-of-void finding from this call.
All five are plain test(), not testWidgets(); FakeAsync microtask-pump warning for testWidgets handlers does not by itself imply these awaits hang.
Test imports existing public FakeBackend fixture, constructs real Session with isAndroid true and injected provider/backend, and does not create native Player or perform open/native codec work.
tearDown resets failure hook, releases held replies, unregisters manual listeners, disposes all Sessions, explicitly disables once, closes call stream, and removes outbound mock.

nonblocking_notes.text: Unchanged constructor comment still says Phase 1 assumes one Session per process. Setter comment now correctly explains listener-owned lifetime. Updating this old comment would improve consistency, but Session is outside this slice and was not edited; this is not a functional blocker.

api_evidence.fact: Getter declared TestDefaultBinaryMessenger and casts inherited getter to that type. Official current API source.
Override returns Future<ByteData?>, supports null callback, returns inbound handler result. Documentation FakeAsync note specifically concerns testWidgets.
Built-in MethodChannel guarantees receive FIFO. invokeMethod<T> returns Future<T?>.

Native/real-device event registration and actual display changes remain DEVICE acceptance. This patch does not prove HDR output, decoder identity, owner/carrier resource lifecycle, sustained performance, or native input acceptance.

Existing Session catchError treats subscription failure as best effort; failed last disable may leave native subscription until an explicit retry/engine teardown. Test documents retry possibility, not an automatic Session retry feature.
No cross-engine ownership protocol added; Dart listener lifetime and native plugin instance are reviewed within one engine/isolate scope.
